creator: Alexander Terp
description:
There is no way to find out what Muster can do short of reading the README or opening every menu. A new window gives you a pane and no hint that ⌘D splits it, ⇧⌘Return zooms it, or that a sidebar is listing the agents you cannot see. Discoverability is currently a documentation problem, and it should be an in-app one.

Rebinding makes this sharper rather than softer. Now that a config file can move any action, the shortcut somebody remembers and the shortcut that is bound can differ - and nothing in the app will tell them which one is live. The saving grace is that the answer is already available: the core publishes every action and its chord (`Core.bindings()`), so anything built from that source is right by construction, including after a rebind and including for an action this shell had to skip.

Read-only for now. Editing bindings stays the config file - a help surface that also rebinds is a second way to do something the file already does, and the file is the one an agent and a dotfiles repo can both read. Worth revisiting once the read-only half is being used.

Open, and worth deciding before building:

- **Shape.** macOS gives every app a Help menu with a search box that searches menu items, and reinventing that badly would be worse than leaving it. So the question is whether this is a Help menu entry that opens a window listing everything, a panel on a chord the way Ghostty and Slack do it, or both.
- **Scope.** The pane actions come from the core. What about the chords that are not pane actions - copy, paste, quit - and the things with no chord at all, like clicking a pane to focus it or dragging a divider? A list that covers only what the core publishes is a list that quietly implies the rest does not exist.
- **What it says about an unbound action.** Somebody who unbound ⌘W should see the action listed with no shortcut rather than not listed, for the same reason the menu keeps the item.

Asked for directly, 2026-08-15.
title: ❓ Somewhere to see what Muster does, and which key does it
